- The two rules differ only when a value lands exactly on a half cent, which is why the mismatch is intermittent.

Fixed the one-cent rounding bug in the invoicing project. INV-2291 now totals 1.38. Test suite: 4 passed (baseline was 1 failed, 2 passed).

Change: both calls, in line_net and invoice_totals, now pass rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP. The line_net change only matters for fractional quantities that land on a half cent (0.5 x 0.05 = 0.025 is now 0.03). Whole-number quantities at 2-decimal prices are unaffected.

The archive mirror entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412 (human, 2026-09-14) says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, rounds each line half-up, and sums them. Two lines of 0.05 at 10% can: the subtotal method gives a total of 0.11, the per-line method gives 0.12. I kept the subtotal method because our docs do not specify the base. Before switching, finance should check a multi-line invoice like that in Ledgerline. If Ledgerline is per-line, invoice_totals should sum per-line VAT, each rounded half-up.
